outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the standard n-conjecture (Browkin and Brzeziński: limsup of the quality equals 2n−5) has not been settled in either half, as far as I can find; its lower-bound half dates from 1994 and its upper bound is still conjectured. In-window events concern variants and the n = 3 case: Hölzl, Kleine and Stephan (arXiv, 20 Sep 2024) disprove Ramaekers' strong variant for every n ≥ 5; a Lean-checked family credited to GPT-6 Astra (repository dated 5–7 Sep 2026) refutes that variant at n = 4 with quality limsup ≥ 9/8; the n = 3 instance, which is abc, saw power-saving exceptional-set bounds in 2024–25 and a 2012 claimed proof that remains disputed.
problem_asks: From the statement alone: (1) a generalization of the abc conjecture; (2) to more than three integers, so for each n ≥ 4 (the n = 3 case is abc itself, which the wording excludes). The statement does not fix the form. Read with the literature it points to (Browkin and Brzeziński 1994, as the Wikipedia 'N conjecture' article and Hölzl–Kleine–Stephan give it): for integers a_1..a_n with gcd 1, a_1+…+a_n = 0 and no vanishing proper subsum, and for every ε > 0, max|a_i| ≤ C(n,ε)·rad(a_1⋯a_n)^(2n−5+ε), equivalently limsup of q = log max|a_i| / log rad(a_1⋯a_n) equals 2n−5. Parts to be settled separately for each n ≥ 4: (a) the lower-bound half, limsup q ≥ 2n−5; (b) the upper-bound half, limsup q ≤ 2n−5 (equivalently the ε-form above). The exponent 2n−5 comes from the literature, not from the statement as frozen; I could not check the January 2024 wording of the Wikipedia article itself (I read the revision last edited 2 Oct 2026). Closely related items the same literature covers, not asked by the statement: Browkin's strong version (pairwise coprime, no subsum condition, conjectured finite quality), Ramaekers' strong version (pairwise coprime, subsum kept, conjectured quality 1), and the n = 3 instance (abc).

events.what_happened: Browkin and Brzeziński, 'Some remarks on the abc-conjecture', Mathematics of Computation 62(206) (1994) 931–939. States the n-conjecture for n ≥ 3 with exponent 2n−5 (Hölzl–Kleine–Stephan Conjecture 2: 'Then Q_A(n)=2n−5 for every n'). Its Theorem 1.3, per the Redhill Lean docstring, gives the lower bound: the quality of the n-tuples is at least 2n−5 (formalised as le_quality_nConjectureTuples). Hölzl–Kleine–Stephan say 'One half of the n-conjecture is known', which is this lower bound. The paper is not accessed by me (AMS page returned 403; JSTOR blocked). A 1993 citation seen in a search snippet places a same-titled Göteborg preprint in 1992; not verified.
events.revisions: Possible 1992 preprint (Göteborg, same title) per a search snippet of a 1993 citation; not verified.
events.delivers: Standard n-conjecture statement for n ≥ 3, and the lower bound limsup q ≥ 2n−5 for every n ≥ 3 (lower half only).
events.remains: The upper bound limsup q ≤ 2n−5 for every n ≥ 3, i.e. the conjectured half. For n = 3 this is abc.

events.what_happened: Pasten and Sepúlveda-Manzo, 'On the abc and the abcd conjectures', arXiv:2406.05083, submitted 7 June 2024 (v1; only version found). Theorem 1.6 (abcd, n = 4): for pairwise coprime nonzero x_1..x_4 with sum zero and H = max|x_j|, assuming min_{i<j}|x_i+x_j| ≤ H/exp((log H)^τ·log₂*H) for some τ > 0, one gets log H ≤ exp(τ⁻¹κ·(log₃*R/log₂*R)·log R) with R = rad(x_1x_2x_3x_4) and κ absolute, so log H ≪_ε R^ε. The paper says 'we are not aware of any unconditional result (not even exponential!) for these conjectures over Z for any n ≥ 4'. It does not prove the exponent 2n−5.
events.delivers: For n = 4 only: an unconditional subexponential bound on max|x_j| in terms of the radical, under a size hypothesis (a pairwise sum is unusually small). Weaker than the conjectured exponent 2n−5 and restricted by hypothesis.
events.remains: The exponent 2n−5 for n = 4 (Q_A(4) ≤ 3 would also give abc, per Hölzl–Kleine–Stephan Remark 5); all n ≥ 5; the case without the size hypothesis.
events.direction: Subexponential bound for n = 4, a weaker form than the conjectured exponent; neither confirms nor refutes the conjectured exponent.

events.what_happened: Hölzl, Kleine and Stephan, 'Improved lower bounds for strong n-conjectures', arXiv:2409.13439 (v1 20 Sep 2024; v2 7 Feb 2025), later J. Aust. Math. Soc. 119 (2025) 61–81 (DOI 10.1017/S1446788725000084; published online 2 Jun 2025). Lower bounds on limsup quality for strong variants on the restricted class U(F,n) (pairwise coprime, stronger subsum condition, forbidden factors F): Theorem 12, Q_U(F,n) ≥ 5/3 for odd n ≥ 5 when 2, 5, 10 ∉ F; Theorem 13, Q_U(F,n) ≥ 5/4 for n ≥ 6 and any finite F; hence Q_R(n) ≥ 5/4 (n ≥ 6) and ≥ 5/3 (odd n ≥ 5). Theorem 14 gives 3/2 at n = 5; Theorem 16 gives Q_U(F,5) > 1 when 5 or 10 may lie in F. The authors state that Ramaekers' conjecture is false for every n ≥ 5. They do not settle n = 3 or n = 4 (Wikipedia: no nontrivial lower bounds for n = 3, 4).
events.revisions: v1 20 Sep 2024; v2 7 Feb 2025; journal version online 2 Jun 2025.
events.delivers: Limsup-quality lower bounds for the restricted class U(F,n) (5/3 for odd n ≥ 5 with 2, 5, 10 ∉ F; 5/4 for n ≥ 6, any finite F), hence the disproof of Ramaekers' strong conjecture (Q_R(n) = 1) for every n ≥ 5. The class U(F,n) lies inside the standard class A(n), so these are lower bounds on the standard quantity Q_A(n) too, but they are weaker than the already-known Q_A(n) ≥ 2n−5 and so change no value of the standard statement.
events.remains: Standard n-conjecture (A(n)): the upper bound limsup Q_A(n) ≤ 2n−5, for every n. Browkin's finiteness Q_B(n) < ∞ (lower bounds are consistent with it). n = 3 (abc) and n = 4 for both strong variants.

events.what_happened: Bernert, Browning, Lichtman and Teräväinen, 'Bounds on the exceptional set in the abc conjecture', arXiv:2410.12234 (v1 16 Oct 2024; v2 9 May 2026). Power-saving bound on the number of coprime triples (a,b,c) in [1,X]^3 with a+b=c and rad(abc) < c^(1−ε), i.e. exceptions to abc for fixed ε. The exponent O(X^(33/50)) is as reported by Li (2025) and a search snippet; I did not find it in the BLT abstract page, which says only 'power-saving bound'. The paper concerns n = 3 only.
events.revisions: v1 16 Oct 2024; v2 9 May 2026 (content not checked).
events.delivers: For the abc case (n = 3 of this family): a power-saving count of exceptional triples, O(X^(33/50)) per later reports. Restricted to n = 3; says nothing about n ≥ 4 or about the sup of the quality.
events.remains: The abc exceptional-set finiteness itself for every ε (the n = 3 instance), and all n ≥ 4. Scope reading: the bullet names n > 3, so n = 3 is outside its words. Whether the exception count is 'a quantity named in the statement' depends on reading the bullet as the family including n = 3, where the count is the conjecture's own quantity (§2.1 abc example).
events.direction: Counts abc exceptions with a power saving. For n = 3 this bounds the exception set; it does not settle the abc statement.

It contains modules BB94 (the 1994 lower bound: le_quality_nConjectureTuples, quality ≥ 2n−5 for n ≥ 3), Common/Conjectures (definitions NConjecture as quality = 2n−5, StrongNConjecture as quality < ⊤, RamaekersConjecture as quality = 1, and a proven nConjecture_3_iff_ABC), Four (the n = 4 refutation, see the Adamczewski entries), Odd and General (strong variants). Commit history on the first page runs from 11 Apr 2026 to 12 Oct 2026. Reservoir shows 'last updated 18 Sep 2026'.

events.what_happened: Repository tadamcz/n-conjecture-strong (github.com/tadamcz/n-conjecture-strong), commits on main dated 5–7 Sep 2026 (15 commits; the earliest is 'Initial import: Hawk run data and analysis (strong n-conjecture, n=4 refutations)', 5 Sep; 'Prove strong four-conjecture false with a 9/8 quality bound' also 5 Sep; 'Add Comparator-format Challenge.lean stating the refuted formulations', 7 Sep). README description: 'Lean 4 counterexample to the n=4 case of the strong n-conjecture (Ramaekers 2009; Hölzl–Kleine–Stephan 2024, Conj. 7)'. Claims: an explicit infinite family of pairwise coprime integer 4-tuples with sum zero whose quality limsup is at least 9/8 (so limsup = 1 fails for Ramaekers' R(4)); the same family disproves every uniform bound for 0 ≤ ε < 1/8. The Wikipedia 'List of mathematical discoveries by artificial intelligence' (last edited 12 Oct 2026) has a row for it (September 2026, number theory, 'Lean formalization', note 'the only remaining open case', AI provenance 'Epoch AI, GPT-6 Astra', citing this repository as 'Lean 4 counterexample to the n=4 case of the strong N conjecture').
events.revisions: 15 commits on main, 5–7 Sep 2026 (commit dates only, times not shown); latest shown 7 Sep 2026 ('Remove redundant Lean audit and add AI authorship note' and earlier docs commits). Commit dates on the page are the only dates; no arXiv preprint or write-up found. Date reads as first public posting, pending the repository's visibility history, which I did not check.
events.delivers: Refutes Ramaekers' strong conjecture at n = 4: an explicit family with quality limsup ≥ 9/8 > 1 among pairwise coprime admissible 4-tuples (HKS Conjecture 7 / Ramaekers R(4)). Restriction: n = 4 only, and the stated claim is a lower bound 9/8, not an equality or convergence (the README says so). Optimality and publication novelty are not claimed. The family is a subset of the standard class A(4), so it gives Q_A(4) ≥ 9/8, far below the conjectured and already-known Q_A(4) ≥ 3; it does not touch the standard upper bound.
events.remains: For the Ramaekers variant: nothing at n = 4 beyond the bound. For the standard n-conjecture: the upper bound for every n, including n = 4 (conjectured limsup 3). Browkin's strong conjecture (finite quality at n = 4) is not addressed (the README does not mention Browkin).

machine_checked.system: Lean 4.27.0 with a pinned Mathlib (repository lean-toolchain and lake-manifest.json)
machine_checked.sorry_free: README: the proof contains no sorry or axiom. Challenge.lean contains sorry by design (a comparator-format statement). I ran no build; the README's build steps are 'lake exe cache get' then 'lake build', plus a Docker route and a Python SymPy check (scripts/check_construction.py).

events.directly_checkable: Yes in principle. The family is given by the identity u^9 − (u−8)^5(u²+20u+280)² − 105(2u−3)^6 + D(u) = 0 (README), with D(u) a polynomial bounded by 1249182732·u⁴ for u ≥ 19 (PROOF.md; D itself not transcribed here). PROOF.md says it comes from the Pakovich–Zvonkin pair P = x⁹, Q = (x−1)⁵(x²+5x/2+35/8)² by subtracting (105/8)(x−3/16)⁶ and substituting x = u/8 and multiplying by 8⁹. Coprimality is by explicit Bézout identities. Indices are u_n with 2u_n − 3 = 35·Kⁿ. A hand check means expanding degree-nine polynomials.
events.doubts: (1) Origin of the construction is attributed inconsistently. The Redhill module docstring says 'This construction was originally found by Tom Adamczewski using GPT-6 Astra.' The repository's own PROOF.md attributes the family to Pakovich–Zvonkin §3 and says 'A bounded search through the binomial-series examples' found it, naming no searcher. The README says 'The Lean proof itself was written by GPT-6 Astra.' Those three statements are not reconciled in any source I read. (2) The README says the 9/8 improves on 'supplied' constructions at 20/19 and 180/179. I could not identify their source, and a value above 1 at n = 4 would sit awkwardly with 'no nontrivial lower bound at n = 4' in the Wikipedia summary of Hölzl–Kleine–Stephan. (3) The 'Hawk run data' in the first commit is not explained anywhere I could read. (4) No human written review found. The repository is five weeks old. (5) The repository's conjecture target is HKS Conjecture 7 (the README says it follows the 'Stronger form' section of the Wikipedia article); the Wikipedia list's citation calls it the 'strong N conjecture'. Both are signals, not verdicts.
events.direction: Refutes Ramaekers' strong conjecture at n = 4 (limsup 1 vs ≥ 9/8). Neutral for the standard n-conjecture, whose conjectured n = 4 value 3 is not contradicted by a lower bound of 9/8.
events.object: An explicit infinite family of pairwise-coprime integer 4-tuples (x_1..x_4) with sum zero, indexed by u_n (2u_n − 3 = 35·Kⁿ), from the polynomial identity in directly_checkable. It shows limsup of log max|x_i| / log rad(x_1x_2x_3x_4) ≥ 9/8 (PROOF.md: for every real q < 9/8, eventually q < log H_n / log R_n). Explicit construction, not an existence proof. The same family disproves every uniform bound max|x_i| ≤ C·rad^(1+ε) for 0 ≤ ε < 1/8.

disputes.summary: Origin of the n = 4 construction. Redhill's docstring says 'originally found by Tom Adamczewski using GPT-6 Astra'; the README says 'The Lean proof itself was written by GPT-6 Astra'; PROOF.md says the family comes from Pakovich–Zvonkin §3 and 'a bounded search through the binomial-series examples', with no searcher named. No source reconciles these.

Whether n = 4 was open before Sept 2026. The Wikipedia summary of Hölzl–Kleine–Stephan says they found no nontrivial lower bound for n = 3 or n = 4. The HKS HTML says Ramaekers 'computed numerous example elements' of R(3), R(4), R(5). The README says the 9/8 improves on 'supplied' constructions at 20/19 and 180/179, whose source I could not identify. If any of those is a quality above 1 at n = 4 for Ramaekers' variant, the 'open at n = 4' status is not clean. Not resolved.

'Strong n-conjecture' names two variants. Browkin's B(n) (pairwise coprime, no subsum condition, finite quality) and Ramaekers' R(n) (pairwise coprime, subsum kept, quality 1). HKS uses the term for both. The Wikipedia article calls the second 'Ramaekers conjecture' under a 'Strong n conjecture' heading. The Wikipedia list row labels the object 'N conjecture (n = 4 case)' but its citation says 'strong N conjecture'.

Scope of the abc instance. Under the bullet's own wording ('more than three integers') n = 3 is excluded, but the literature's family includes n = 3 as abc. Under that reading the 2012 Mochizuki claim, the 2024–25 exceptional-set counts and the 2026 LANA report bear on the family; under the bullet's wording they do not. Recorded both ways for the judging pass.

summary:
The standard n-conjecture (Browkin and Brzeziński 1994) says that for n ≥ 3, the limsup of q = log max|a_i| / log rad(a_1⋯a_n) equals 2n−5. The lower-bound half is a 1994 theorem: Redhill formalises it in Lean as Theorem 1.3 of that paper, and Hölzl–Kleine–Stephan write 'One half of the n-conjecture is known'. I could not open the 1994 paper itself (AMS returned 403; JSTOR blocked). The upper-bound half is conjectured. Hölzl–Kleine–Stephan (arXiv 2409.13439) state it as Conjecture 2, the Wikipedia article (last edited 2 Oct 2026) calls it open, and Redhill defines it in Lean as an equality without proving the upper half. I found no proof or disproof of the upper bound for any n in the window.

What moved in the window concerns variants and the n = 3 case. (a) Hölzl, Kleine and Stephan (20 Sep 2024) show Browkin–Brzeziński-type lower bounds for restricted strong variants (5/3 for odd n ≥ 5, 5/4 for n ≥ 6) and so disprove Ramaekers' strong variant (limsup quality = 1) for every n ≥ 5. Those bounds sit below the known 2n−5 lower bound, so they change no value of the standard statement. (b) Adamczewski's repository (5–7 Sep 2026) gives an explicit family of pairwise coprime integer 4-tuples with quality limsup ≥ 9/8, which refutes Ramaekers' variant at n = 4. The README says the Lean proof was written by GPT-6 Astra; the same repository's PROOF.md says the family comes from Pakovich–Zvonkin §3 and a bounded search, without naming a searcher; the Redhill module docstring says the construction was originally found by Adamczewski using GPT-6 Astra. Redhill ports it into Lean (15–18 Sep 2026) and says the port used no LLM. The Wikipedia AI list has a row for it ('Lean formalization', 'the only remaining open case', provenance 'Epoch AI, GPT-6 Astra'). No written human review was found. For the standard statement the result is inert: its family is a subset of the standard class and its 9/8 sits below the known 3 at n = 4.

The n = 3 instance is abc. Mochizuki's IUT papers (August 2012, by the best-supported date) claim it; the claim is disputed (Scholze–Stix 2018; the LANA interim report of 17 Jul 2026 says the Theorem 3.11→Corollary 3.12 step cannot be formalised as written, with no verdict). Three exceptional-set papers, all n = 3 only (BLT Oct 2024 with X^(33/50); Bernert June 2025; Li June 2025 with X^(56/85+ε)), bound abc exceptions with a power saving. On the bullet's wording (more than three integers) these are outside scope; on the literature's family (n = 3 included) the exception count is the conjecture's own quantity. Both readings are recorded.

Calls that were close: whether the bullet denotes the standard statement or the variant family; whether the Adamczewski family was AI-originated or AI-written (the sources disagree); whether the 20/19 and 180/179 constructions in the README make n = 4 'open' untrue for the Ramaekers variant. None of these changes the standard statement's status.
competing_reading: Read the bullet as the family that Wikipedia's 'N conjecture' article covers, which includes the 'strong' Ramaekers variant. Then the family moved twice in the window: HKS (Sep 2024) disproved the variant for n ≥ 5, and the Sep 2026 n = 4 refutation, credited in part to GPT-6 Astra and Lean-checked, closes the only remaining case of that variant (per the Wikipedia list's note). That reading makes this item an AI-involved move, and one in which the AI attribution is contested. Read the bullet as the Browkin–Brzeziński statement (upper bound limsup = 2n−5): nothing in the window moves it, and the AI-credited result does not touch it. A third reading includes n = 3, so that the 2012 claim and the 2024–25 exceptional-set counts count as well.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The judging pass fixes which statement the bullet denotes: the standard Browkin–Brzeziński limsup = 2n−5, or the family including Ramaekers' and Browkin's strong variants, and whether n = 3 is included. (2) For the AI item: who or what found the n = 4 family. The 'Hawk run data' in the first commit of tadamcz/n-conjecture-strong, or a statement by the repository's author, would settle it. (3) A lake build of tadamcz/n-conjecture-strong and of Redhill, plus a hand expansion of the degree-nine identity, to confirm the sorry-free claims. I did not run these. (4) The source of the 20/19 and 180/179 constructions for n = 4. (5) For the standard statement, any proof or disproof of limsup Q_A(n) ≤ 2n−5 for any n. None found.

incomplete: (1) The 1994 Browkin–Brzeziński paper was not accessed (AMS 403; JSTOR blocked). Its statement and the lower bound are taken from Hölzl–Kleine–Stephan and the Redhill docstring. (2) The Browkin 2000 proceedings volume was not accessed; its date and content come from secondary references. (3) The Ramaekers 2009 thesis PDF is binary and unreadable with WebFetch; its existence is supported by the Wikipedia reference list, a ResearchGate title, and the tadamcz README link, not by reading the text. The claims about its Conjecture 5.1 and its computed examples come from the README and the HKS summary. (4) The stephan slides and strong n-conjecture PDF are binary and unreadable; the 'Computer Search' section in the slide bookmarks was not read. (5) The 20/19 and 180/179 constructions in the Adamczewski README have no identified source. (6) The Adamczewski and Redhill repositories were read through WebFetch's summarising fetch of the raw files, not by clone, grep or build. Quotations are as the fetch returned them and were not checked character by character. Sorry-free status, the lake build and the Python check are unverified. The degree-nine identity was not hand-checked and D(u) is not transcribed. (7) The origin of the n = 4 family (Astra vs bounded search) is unresolved. The 'Hawk run data' referred to in the first commit is unexplained, and I found no run logs. (8) The OpenAI announcement (1 Aug 2026) was not opened (403); the 'unreleased internal model' description of Astra comes from search summaries. (9) The Mochizuki claim, the LANA report and the Joshi critique were not opened; the 2012 date conflicts between August and September sources. (10) The BLT exponent 33/50 is not verified in BLT's own text. Bernert's main theorem was not read. The journal acceptance date for Hölzl–Kleine–Stephan was not seen. (11) The Wikipedia pages read are the October 2026 revisions, not the frozen January 2024 revision. (12) Search coverage is limited to the web index available to me; no MathSciNet, zbMATH, Google Scholar or arXiv full-text search was available, and no later independent review of the n = 4 claim was found. (13) The Google formal-conjectures check covered only 'Browkin'.
